#left_join() keeps the left table whole and adds the right table's columns. Where no partner exists, the new cells are NA, which is a fact worth knowing, not an error.

#Joins in practice
```{r}
states = tibble::tibble(location_state = state.abb,
                        state_name = state.name,
                        region = as.character(state.region))
jobs |>
  dplyr::left_join(states, by = "location_state") |>
  dplyr::group_by(region) |>
  dplyr::summarize(postings = dplyr::n(), remote_share = mean(remote)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(postings))
```



#AirBNB practice
```{r}
con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "../data/midwest_airbnb.db")
listings = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "listings") |>
  tibble::as_tibble()
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
dplyr::glimpse(listings)

#Listings per city
#I can group by city and count number of listings in each

listings |> dplyr::group_by(city) |> dplyr::summarise(count=dplyr::n()) 

#The shortcut for the code above 

listings |> dplyr::count(city) #count does group by and then n ()

#another option is to count number of times each city occurred in the city column

table(listings$city) #returns a named vector vs above is a data frame

#For entire homes (room_type == "Entire home/apt") that sleep four or more, what is the median price in each city?

listings |> 
  dplyr::filter(room_type=="Entire home/apt", accommodates>=4
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median_price=median(price)
  )

#Which 3 listings are the cheapest per person
#for the sake of printing nicely, reduce # of columns

listings |>
  dplyr::mutate(price_per_person=price/accommodates) |>
  dplyr::select(city, host_name, name, accommodates, price_per_person) |>
  dplyr::arrange(price_per_person)


#What 5 host names have most listings, host names are not unique but host ids are

listings|>
  dplyr::count(host_name, sort=T)


#groups by both host name and host id to try to find unique host
listings|>
  dplyr::count(host_name, host_id, sort=T)
```


#API step-by-step
```{r}
httr2::request("https://data.cincinnati-oh.gov/resource/rvmt-pkmq.json") |> #Specifies request to get data from that link
  httr2::req_url_query("$limit" = 5) |> #Reconstructs URL for limit=5
  httr2::req_perform() |> #Executing request
  httr2::resp_body_string() |> #Response in a string
  jsonlite::fromJSON() -> cincy_crashes
```
